items.description: Cameroon's main commercial port on the Wouri estuary. It handles most of the country's seaborne imports and exports.
A modern deep-sea port on Cameroon's southern coast. It was built to handle large cargo ships and ease pressure on Douala.
A smaller Atlantic port in the Bay of Ambas. It supports fishing, local shipping, and coastal trade.
Cameroon's only oil refinery, located in Limbe. It processes crude oil for the domestic fuel market.
A major aluminum smelter in Edea. It relies on hydroelectric power from the Sanaga basin.
One of Cameroon's classic hydro plants on the Sanaga River. It supports local industry and the national grid.
One of Cameroon's largest hydroelectric facilities on the Sanaga River. Its output feeds the national electricity network.
A hydroelectric dam in southern Cameroon on the Ntem River. It adds power capacity and strengthens the grid.
A regulating and storage dam in eastern Cameroon on the Lom River. It helps balance flows in the Sanaga system.
A gold-mining area in eastern Cameroon near Betare Oya. Small-scale and industrial extraction both shape the local economy.
A cobalt-nickel mining project in eastern Cameroon near Lomie. It is often cited among the country's strategic mineral deposits.
A major iron-ore deposit in southeastern Cameroon near Mbalam. It remains part of the country's long-term mining plans.
